messages.subject_clean: DIF function runs for infinity
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to run a DIF analysis on multidimensional nominal data.
I am using the guide written by Adam Meade - he wrote the guide on Likert data with one dimension, but I'm trying to adapt it to my problem.

When I'm running the DIF function, the function runs for infinity - I left it to run all night and nothing happened in the morning.

I first run the multipleGroup function to create a baseline model:

model.constrained <- multipleGroup(data, 3, group,
                                  invariance = c(colnames(data), 'free_means', 'free_var'))

This one runs for 500 iterations and then shows the warning: "EM cycles terminated after 500 iterations." but the object is still created so I used it in the DIF function.
I run the DIF function like this:

dif.drop <- DIF(model.constrained, c('a1','a2','a3','d1','d2','d3'), scheme = 'drop',
                seq_stat = .05)

And it runs for infinity times. I tried playing with the max_run parameter of the function but it doesn't help.

Anyone have any suggestions on what's the problem and what I can do to solve it?

Thanks!

messages.subject_clean: findnextitem doesn't check criterion?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

i use mirtCAT as a backend in a server and wrote a function that takes a response vector, updates the CAT with these responses and returns the next item. However, the function will always return an item and doesn't return NA when the criterion for the CAT is fulfilled. Am I missing an additional step besides  xx$des...@Update.thetas(xx$design, xx$person, xx$test) to update the criteria check?

Best, Felix

set.seed(1234)
nitems <- 50
itemnames <- paste0('Item.', 1:nitems)
a <- matrix(rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3))
d <- matrix(rnorm(nitems))
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = 'dich')
mod <- mirt(dat, 1)
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)

# simple math items
questions <- answers <- character(nitems)
choices <- matrix(NA, nitems, 5)
spacing <- floor(d - min(d)) + 1 #easier items have more variation in the options

for(i in 1:nitems){
  n1 <- sample(1:50, 1)
  n2 <- sample(51:100, 1)
  ans <- n1 + n2
  questions[i] <- paste0(n1, ' + ', n2, ' = ?')
  answers[i] <- as.character(ans)
  ch <- ans + sample(c(-5:-1, 1:5) * spacing[i,], 5)
  ch[sample(1:5, 1)] <- ans
  choices[i, ] <- as.character(ch)
}

df <- data.frame(Question=questions, Option=choices,
                 Type = 'radio', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

xx = mirtCAT(mo = mod, df = df, design_elements = TRUE, design = list(min_SEM =.8))

for (i in 1:30){
  xx <- updateDesign(xx, items = i, responses = 1)
  xx$des...@Update.thetas(xx$design, xx$person, xx$test)
}

findnextitem(xx)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Felix,

The NA return option from findNextItem() is mainly useful when front-end users are supplying their own customNextItem definition. By default, it just finds the next item regardless of the stopping criteria (excluding running out of the item bank entirely). If it helps, see the local run function for mirtCAT which is used to evaluate CAT designs without the GUI:

https://github.com/philchalmers/mirtCAT/blob/master/R/run_pattern.R

Perhaps what you are looking for is the internal Update.stop_now() function, which I'd be happy to wrap inside one of the objects to make available (like putting this in Des...@Update.stop_now()). HTH.

Phil

messages.subject_clean: Loading reversed when fitted to samples of the same population
messages.body_plain:
You should be able to just modify the starting values via the three-step mod2values() to make the model converge more towards the orientation you want. Latent variable models will fit exactly the same if some/all of the loads are reversed, so you probably want the optimizer to stay way form this behaviour. I don't know what kind of model you are running (EFA vs CFA, or the itemtypes), but that's the general strategy.

Phil
